breaks.what: Higher-priced loan threshold changes (October 2009): rate spreads are measured against a new benchmark, so the high-priced share before and after isn't comparable.
Census tracts switch from 2000 to 2010 boundaries; tract demographics switch to the 2010 census and ACS. The maps put every year on 2020 tracts.

The 2015 HMDA rule takes effect: debt-to-income, combined LTV, property value, credit-score model, underwriting system, age, interest rate and loan costs are added; denial reasons become required; cash-out refinances and second homes are reported separately; open-end lines, reverse mortgages and business loans are flagged (and excluded here); race and ethnicity subgroups are added (folded back into the main groups here); loan amounts are rounded to $10,000 bands. Small lenders may be exempt from the new fields.
Reporting threshold for closed-end loans rises from 25 to 100 originations a year, so the smallest lenders drop out of the data.
